title: Stratum 1 · timepi
description: GPS-disciplined NTP/PTP time server timepi: ntpsec, gpsd, kernel PPS, ptp4l/phc2sys, the fleet that syncs from it, and the hardware under the clock.

panels.title: Disciplined by
panels.description: Whether ntpd follows the GPS PPS refclock (SHM 1) as its system peer. Anything else means it fell back to the internet pool or has no source.

panels.title: Stratum
panels.description: 1: synchronised to a reference clock. 16: unsynchronised.

panels.title: Leap
panels.description: Leap indicator ntpd announces: none, a leap second pending (insert/delete) or unsynchronised (3).

panels.title: PPS offset
panels.description: Offset of the PPS refclock to the system clock as ntpd measures it (16 s poll). Green within ±10 µs, amber within ±100 µs.

panels.title: PPS jitter
panels.description: RMS jitter of the PPS refclock's offsets.

panels.title: PPS signal
panels.description: Pulses per second the kernel counts on /dev/pps0. 1 Hz: the receiver's PPS is wired and present.

panels.title: GPS fix
panels.description: gpsd's fix mode. The PPS edges need a fix to be numbered.

panels.title: Satellites used
panels.description: Satellites in the fix (of those in view). Timing needs one once the position is known; four for a 3D fix.

panels.title: PTP port
panels.description: ptp4l's port state on eth0. As grandmaster it should be MASTER.

panels.title: PTP clock class
panels.description: clockClass ptp4l announces. 6: locked to a primary reference (GPS); 7: holdover; 248: default (not traceable). Configured, not measured: ptp4l announces what ptp4l.conf says.

panels.title: PHC ↔ system
panels.description: RMS offset of eth0's hardware clock to the system clock over the last minute (phc2sys).

panels.title: NTP clients (1 h)
panels.description: Distinct addresses that asked timepi for time in the last hour (ntpd's MRU list). The fleet has 14 ntp-client hosts; the PTP slaves may not ask over NTP at all.

panels.title: Requests served
panels.description: Requests from LAN clients since their MRU entries were created (about since ntpd started).

panels.title: Root distance
panels.description: Root delay/2 + root dispersion: the error bound timepi advertises to its clients.

panels.title: Leap file expires
panels.description: When /usr/share/zoneinfo/leap-seconds.list expires (tzdata updates renew it). Past expiry ntpd ignores it and can miss a leap second.

panels.title: ntpd up
panels.description: Time since ntpd started (its statistics reset).

panels.title: Offset to GPS
panels.description: How far the system clock is from the GPS second. PPS refclock: ntpd's filtered measurement every 16 s. Kernel PPS timestamp: the system time the kernel stamped on the last pulse, read every 30 s (the raw, unfiltered view, including interrupt latency). System offset (dashed): what the discipline loop is steering out; with PPS as the only selected source it equals the PPS offset.

panels.title: Offset distribution (PPS refclock)
panels.description: Distribution of ntpd's PPS offsets over the selected time range. A narrow peak centred on 0 is a well-disciplined clock; a skew or second peak points at temperature swings or interrupt latency.

panels.title: Jitter
panels.description: PPS refclock: RMS of its offsets. System jitter: spread of the selected sources. Clock jitter: RMS of the system clock's recent offsets.

panels.title: Frequency correction
panels.description: How fast ntpd has to slew the system clock to keep it on GPS time: the crystal's error. It moves with temperature (see Hardware). 1 ppm = 86 ms/day if left uncorrected. Read from the kernel (adjtimex), where ntpd sets it.

panels.title: Frequency stability (Allan deviation)
panels.description: Allan deviation of the kernel frequency correction ntpd sets, which tracks the crystal's fractional frequency: how much the average frequency over τ differs from the next τ (rolling over 2 h / 6 h / 24 h). Lower is a more stable oscillator; growth with τ is temperature-driven wander. ntpd's own clock wander estimate for comparison.

panels.title: Error budget
panels.description: What timepi tells clients about its own error. Root dispersion grows between refclock updates; the kernel's maximum error is what ntpd hands adjtimex.

panels.title: NMEA timing (serial)
panels.description: The NMEA second arrives over 9600 baud serial well after the PPS edge, which is why ntpd never selects the NMEA refclock (noselect); gpsd only uses it to number the pulses. gpsd's view (TOFF) and ntpd's (its NMEA refclock offset with the 0.6 s fudge taken back out) should agree.

targets.legendFormat: NMEA sentence arrival after the second

matcher.options: NMEA sentence arrival after the second

panels.title: Kernel clock (timex)
panels.description: The kernel discipline's remaining offset and its estimated error (adjtimex), as node_exporter reads them. ntpd feeds the kernel PLL; kernel PPS (hardpps) is not used, so the PPS timex counters stay 0.

panels.title: Satellites over the Earth
panels.description: Where each satellite in view is overhead right now (its sub-satellite point), worked out from its azimuth and elevation, the receiver's own fix and its constellation's orbit height. Blue: used in the fix; grey: in view but not used; size: signal strength. The orange marker is timepi's own GPS position.

panels.title: Sky
panels.description: Where the satellites in view are: north up, east right, centre is overhead, the edge the horizon. Axes are degrees from overhead. Size: signal strength; blue: used in the fix, grey: not used.

panels.title: Signal per satellite
panels.description: Carrier-to-noise (C/N0) of every satellite with a signal. Blue: used in the fix; grey: tracked but not used. Above ~35 dB-Hz is a clear view; below ~20 the receiver struggles.

panels.title: Satellites
panels.description: Satellites the almanac puts in view, those with a measurable signal, and those used in the fix.

panels.title: Used per constellation
panels.description: Satellites in the fix by system.

panels.title: Dilution of precision
panels.description: How the satellite geometry amplifies measurement error. TDOP is the one that matters for time. Below 2 is good, above 5 poor.

panels.title: Estimated error
panels.description: The receiver's 95% position error estimate (gpsd eph/epv). For a fixed antenna it mostly reflects sky view and multipath.

panels.title: Fix
panels.description: gpsd fix mode over time.

panels.title: PPS
panels.description: Kernel PPS pulse rate on /dev/pps0.

panels.title: Reference clocks
panels.description: ntpd's verdict on the two refclocks. PPS should be the system peer throughout; the NMEA refclock is noselect, so it is always rejected.

panels.title: Pool servers by verdict
panels.description: The internet pool servers ntpd keeps as fallback, by verdict. Next to the PPS they disagree by milliseconds, so they are outliers; one becoming system peer means the PPS was lost.

panels.title: Pool servers vs GPS
panels.description: Offset of the internet pool servers relative to GPS time (median and spread over the reachable ones). Mostly the asymmetry of the internet path, bounded by half the round trip. The PPS refclock is the truth here.

panels.title: NTP traffic
panels.description: All NTP packets: client requests and answers, plus ntpd's own polls of the pool servers.

panels.title: Dropped and refused
panels.description: Packets ntpd refused or could not send. Flat zero is healthy.

panels.title: Refclock reach
panels.description: Share of the refclocks' last 8 polls (16 s each) that delivered a sample.

panels.title: Worst client offset
panels.description: Largest |system time offset| chrony reports among the hosts that sync from timepi.

panels.title: via PTP
panels.description: Hosts whose chrony follows eth0's PHC, disciplined by ptp4l from timepi.

panels.title: via NTP
panels.description: Hosts whose chrony follows an NTP server (timepi: 192.168.0.109).

panels.title: Client offsets
panels.description: |system time offset| chrony reports on the client hosts, split by what they follow: PTP slaves (chrony on eth0's PHC, which ptp4l keeps on timepi) and NTP clients polling timepi. Log scale.

panels.title: RMS offset by host
panels.description: chrony's long-term RMS offset on each client.

panels.title: PTP slaves: offset to timepi (ptp4l)
panels.description: Offset of each PTP slave's hardware clock to timepi's, as its ptp4l measures it.

panels.title: PTP slaves: path delay
panels.description: Mean path delay to timepi each slave measures (half the round trip through the switch).

panels.title: Source per host
panels.description: What each client's chrony follows: PTP (eth0's PHC) or NTP (timepi over the LAN). A gap: chrony has no reference.

panels.title: Clients
panels.description: Each client: what chrony follows and how well (chrony tracking), its ptp4l view if it is a PTP slave, and when timepi's ntpd last heard from it over NTP (MRU list, matched by reverse DNS).

panels.title: PHC ↔ system clock (phc2sys)
panels.description: How closely phc2sys keeps eth0's hardware clock (which ptp4l serves) on the system clock, from its per-second log lines summarised per minute.

panels.title: PHC frequency (phc2sys)
panels.description: Frequency correction phc2sys applies to eth0's hardware clock: the PHC oscillator's error relative to the GPS-disciplined system clock.

panels.title: PTP messages sent
panels.description: What ptp4l sends as master. Delay_Req arrivals mean someone on the LAN is actually syncing over PTP; zero means no PTP clients.

panels.title: Port state and announced quality
panels.description: ptp4l's port state and the quality it announces to its slaves: clockClass (6: locked to GPS), whether time is traceable and whether the UTC offset is valid. These come from ptp4l.conf, so they say what timepi claims, not what it measures.

panels.title: Grandmaster
panels.description: The grandmaster identity ptp4l sees (its own clock as long as it is the best master on the LAN).

panels.title: Frequency vs SoC temperature
panels.description: Each dot is five minutes: SoC temperature against ntpd's frequency correction. The crystal sits next to the SoC, so a slope here is its temperature coefficient: the main source of wander.

panels.title: SoC temperature
panels.description: SoC temperature (vcgencmd). Its swings show up as frequency changes a few minutes later.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: CPU load heats the SoC and adds interrupt latency to the PPS timestamps.

panels.title: Clocksource
panels.description: The kernel clocksource the system clock reads (arch_sys_counter: the ARM generic timer).

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Since the last boot.

panels.title: CPU clock
panels.description: Current ARM core clock (rpi_exporter reports kHz under a _hertz name, hence the * 1000).

panels.title: Collector
panels.description: Whether every time-metrics source (ntpsec, gpsd, PPS, PTP) answered on the last run.

panels.title: Time daemons (last 24 h)
panels.description: Journal of gpsd, ntpd, ptp4l, phc2sys and the metrics collector over the last day (they are quiet when all is well). phc2sys's per-second offset lines are left out: they are summarised in the PTP row.
